title.narrative: Inclusive Access and Dignified Participation of Persons with Disabilities in Humanitarian Services in Fune LGA, Yobe State.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtProtection Without Borders proposes a 9-month disability inclusion intervention titled “Inclusive Access and Dignified Participation of Persons with Disabilities in Humanitarian Services in Fune Local Government Area, Yobe State.”ltbrgtIn line with the Nigerian Humanitarian Fund requirement that persons with disabilities constitute at least 16 per cent of total direct beneficiaries, the project will directly benefit 2,566 persons with disabilities and their caregivers, representing a minimum of 16 per cent of the total direct project population (approximately 16,040 individuals). The project will indirectly reach an estimated 65,200 community members through a multi-sectoral, community-driven approach promoting equitable access to protection, health, education, water, sanitation and hygiene, and other essential services.ltbrgtThe intervention responds to the 2025 Nigerian Humanitarian Fund Priority Envelope on Disability Inclusion by addressing systemic exclusion, environmental and physical barriers, weak disability-disaggregated data, and discriminatory attitudes that marginalize persons with disabilities in humanitarian settings.ltbrgtBuilding on Protection Without Borders’ experience in disability programming, protection outreach, community engagement, and case management, the project applies a rights-based approach to reduce physical, social, and institutional barriers while promoting participation, resilience, and safety. The intervention integrates disability identification, inclusive access to services, accessibility improvements, community engagement, and capacity strengthening, supported by strong monitoring, accountability, learning, and coordination systems.ltbrgtStandardized disability identification questions will be applied across all identification processes to strengthen disability-disaggregated data and guide referrals. Inclusive service delivery will be supported through mobile outreach, home-based follow-up for individuals with mobility limitations, strengthened referral pathways, and accessible information channels, with a focus on women and girls with disabilities through safe referrals and gender-based violence risk mitigation.ltbrgtThe project will provide assistive and mobility devices, including wheelchairs, crutches, white canes, tricycles, hearing devices, and communication boards, alongside small-scale accessibility upgrades such as ramps, handrails, widened entrances, tactile indicators, and accessible water and sanitation facilities. Community Disability Inclusion Committees will lead stigma-reduction initiatives, facilitate community feedback, and support meaningful participation in local governance and humanitarian planning through accessible complaint and feedback mechanisms.ltbrgtFor sustainability, the project will train 150 frontline workers and community actors, including health personnel, teachers, humanitarian responders, community leaders, volunteers, and government staff, on disability-inclusive communication, accessible service delivery, protection mainstreaming, gender-based violence mitigation, inclusive security, and safeguarding. Institutional support will be provided to the Yobe State Commission for Persons with Disabilities, alongside advocacy for disability rights implementation and strengthened coordination across key humanitarian sectors.ltbrgtAligned with the Inter-Agency Standing Committee Guidelines on the Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities in Humanitarian Action, the Humanitarian Inclusion Standards, and the 2025 Nigerian Humanitarian Fund requirements, the project embeds a strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning framework to advance inclusive, dignified, and sustainable humanitarian outcomes in Fune Local Government Area.lt/pgt
